Il tumore neuroepiteliale disembrioplast:
Dysembryoplastic neuroepithelial tumor (DNET, WHO grade 1) is a benign glioneuronal tumor of the cortex, typical of children and young adults with drug-resistant focal epilepsy, often temporal. On MRI: cortical-subcortical lesion with sharp margins, markedly hyperintense on T2 with a "bubbly" or multicystic appearance, hyperintense rim sign on FLAIR, no edema, little mass effect, rare enhancement; it may remodel the inner table of the skull.
In this case the lesion is oval with homogeneous signal, without the typical "bubbly" appearance and without skull remodeling: the diagnosis rests on cortical location, sharp margins, absence of edema and age.
Differential diagnosis with ganglioglioma (enhancing solid component, calcifications) and focal cortical dysplasia. Treatment is resection, which often cures the epilepsy.
Practical rule: in a young patient with epilepsy, look for small cortical lesions by scrolling through all the images, with thin FLAIR and T2.
